safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies no past psychiatric history/significant anxiety (pmh-001), not 'no past medical history'. Transcript does not establish absence of all PMH; it only addresses prior similar anxiety episodes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting "no past medical history" overstates what was elicited (only no prior similar anxiety episodes), and could cause clinicians to miss or deprioritize relevant comorbidities (e.g., thyroid disease, arrhythmia history) when evaluating anxiety/palpitations. This may lead to incomplete assessment or delayed recognition of non-psychiatric contributors.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Allergy/documentation status is not provided in Gold or transcript.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating "allergies not documented" is largely an administrative/record-quality statement and does not introduce a specific incorrect allergy or contraindication. While it reflects missing information, it is unlikely by itself to directly change immediate clinical decisions in this encounter.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold assessment is 'work-related anxiety' and 'insomnia' (asm-001; asm-002). Transcript/Gold do not diagnose GAD; adding 'GAD' exceeds source. Other elements (work-related anxiety/insomnia/anhedonia) are supported, but the diagnostic label makes the combined fact unsupported.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Labeling the presentation as GAD (when the source supports work-related anxiety/insomnia) can misclassify the condition, potentially influencing treatment choices (e.g., unnecessary pharmacotherapy), follow-up urgency, and stigma/coding. The clinical picture remains anxiety-related, but the incorrect formal diagnosis can lead to clinically meaningful downstream management differences.
